wars.name: Byzantine–Ottoman wars
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Bursa 1326, Karesi 1345-6, Çimpe 1354, Adrianople 1362-3, Thessaloniki 1387 and 1430, Constantinople on 29 May 1453; the emperor is a vassal from 1371.
wars.note: Bapheus (1301 or 1302) is the first battle named; the Interregnum (1402-1413) interrupts the advance.

wars.name: Battle of Kosovo
wars.outcome: On 15 June 1389 both armies were 'largely destroyed'; the Serbian principalities became Ottoman vassals in the following years (Stefan Lazarević in 1390).

wars.name: Crusade of Nicopolis
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory; Vidin is annexed and 'Bulgaria ceased to exist'.

wars.name: Ottoman Interregnum

zones.text: Anatolia east of Bursa, and Macedonia

wars.outcome: After Timur's victory at Ankara (1402) the beyliks regained their lands and the sons of Bayezid fought until Mehmed I defeated Musa outside Sofia in 1413.
wars.note: Mehmed took Sofia and Niš in 1412 and Wallachia was recovered as a vassal in 1419.

wars.name: Crusade of Varna
wars.outcome: Murad II won at Varna on 10 November 1444; a peace of 1448 gave the Ottomans Wallachia, Bulgaria and part of Albania.
wars.note: Niš and Sofia 'fell to the Christians in 1443'; a treaty of 12 July 1444 gave western Bulgaria, including Sofia, to Serbia.

wars.name: Fall of Constantinople
wars.outcome: Mehmed II took Constantinople on 29 May 1453 after a siege that began in April; the Byzantine Empire ended.

wars.name: First Ottoman–Venetian War
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Negroponte, Lemnos and Albania Veneta captured (the page gives no separate dates).

wars.name: Second Ottoman–Venetian War

zones.text: the Venetian strongholds in the Morea

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Venice's strongholds in the Morea captured.

wars.name: Ottoman–Mamluk War (1516–1517)

zones.text: Syria, Palestine, Egypt and the Hejaz

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory at Marj Dabiq (24 August 1516) and Ridaniya (24 January 1517); the Mamluk Sultanate is annexed, Syria, Egypt and the Hejaz become provinces and the caliphate passes to the Ottomans.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1532–1555)

zones.text: Iraq, Western Armenia and western Kurdistan

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Baghdad taken in 1535; the Peace of Amasya (1555) 'partitions the Caucasus; Western Armenia, western Kurdistan, and Western Georgia go to the Ottomans'.
wars.note: The Ottoman-Persian wars page gives only the dates and the result; the territory is from the main article.

wars.name: Third Ottoman–Venetian War

zones.text: the last Venetian strongholds in the Morea

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory; Venice surrenders most of its Aegean and Morea possessions in 1540.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of Hungary
wars.outcome: Mohács (1526) puts about a third of central Hungary under tribute; Buda falls in 1541 and the Ottomans hold the central and southern counties, the Habsburgs the west and north, Transylvania the east; in 1547 Ferdinand recognises Ottoman ascendancy.
wars.note: Vienna was besieged in 1529 and the attack repulsed at Güns in 1532.

wars.name: Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–1573)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Nicosia besieged 22 July 1570, Famagusta falls in August 1571; the fleet is beaten at Lepanto (1571) and peace is made in 1573.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1578–1590)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: the Treaty of Constantinople (1590).
wars.note: No land terms on the page; the Eyalet page creates the Tiflis, Shervan, Yerevan and Tabriz eyalets in 1578-1585.

wars.name: Long Turkish War
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Zsitvatorok (1606) ended it; the war 'did not yield significant territorial changes'. Eger fell in 1596; by 1605 only Raab remained in Austrian hands.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1603–1618)
wars.outcome: Persian victory: the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha (1612) ceded the Caucasus, except westernmost Georgia; the Treaty of Serav (1618) confirmed it.
wars.note: Dedicated page read after review: Tabriz and Nakhchivan October 1603, Yerevan June 1604, Ganja, Baku and Shirvan June 1606, the Treaty of Nasuh Pasha on 20 November 1612.

wars.name: Ottoman–Safavid War (1623–1639)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Baghdad lost on 14 January 1624, retaken in December 1638; the Treaty of Zuhab (17 May 1639) leaves the Ottomans Baghdad and all Mesopotamia, western Georgia, Western Armenia and Samtskhe, and the Safavids Eastern Armenia (Revan), Dagestan, Shirvan and eastern Georgia.

wars.name: Cretan War (1645–1669)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: Crete conquered ('completed' in 1669); Venice loses Dalmatia, Aegean islands and Crete.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1663–1664)
wars.outcome: The Ottomans conquered Nové Zámky (Uyvar) in 1663; the war ended at the Battle of St. Gotthard (1664), a Christian victory.

wars.name: Great Turkish War
wars.outcome: Habsburg-led Holy League victory: Buda reconquered in 1686, the Morea taken by Venice, and the Treaty of Karlowitz (26 January 1699) gives the Austrians the rest of Hungary and overlordship of Transylvania; Podolia returns to Poland.
wars.note: Zenta (11 September 1697) was the decisive defeat; the Venetian wars page does not mention Karlowitz.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1676–1681)
wars.outcome: Disputed; the Treaty of Bakhchisarai 'established the Russo-Turkish border on the Dnieper River'.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1686–1700)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Constantinople (1700) gives Russia Azov, Taganrog, Pavlovsk and Mius.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1710–1711)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory on the Pruth: Russia returned Azov (treaties of Pruth and Adrianople, 1713).

wars.name: Ottoman–Venetian War (1714–1718)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory: the Morea, Tinos and Aigina recaptured, 'the last Venetian holdings in the Aegean'.

wars.name: Austro-Turkish War (1716–1718)
wars.outcome: Habsburg victory: Prince Eugene wins at Petrovaradin (1716) and takes Belgrade (1717); Passarowitz (1718) gives the Austrians the Banat of Temeswar, Serbia and Oltenia.

wars.name: Ottoman–Persian War (1730–1735)
wars.outcome: Persian victory; Treaty of Constantinople (1736).
wars.note: The 1723-1727 Ottoman campaigns in Persia are not on the page.

wars.name: Austro-Russian–Turkish War (1735–1739)

zones.text: Serbia, the southern Banat and northern Bosnia

wars.outcome: Ottoman gains from Austria: the Treaty of Belgrade (1739) returns Serbia with Belgrade, the southern Banat and northern Bosnia, with the Sava and Danube as the line; Oltenia goes to Wallachia. Azov passes to Russia (Treaty of Niš).

wars.name: Ottoman–Persian War (1743–1746)
wars.outcome: Indecisive; Treaty of Kerden (1746).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1768–1774)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Küçük Kaynarca cedes Kerch, Enikale, Kabardia and part of Yedisan; the Crimean Khanate becomes formally independent.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1787–1792)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Jassy (1792) gives Russia Ozi (Ochakov) and the Dniester frontier; Austria's Sistova gains (1791) were 'meager' (Orșova and two small towns).

wars.name: Serbian Revolution
wars.outcome: Serbia wins autonomy; its 'suzerainty as a hereditary monarchy' is acknowledged de jure in 1830.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806–1812)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: Bucharest (1812) gives Russia Bessarabia.

wars.name: Ottoman–Saudi War (1811–1818)
wars.outcome: Muhammad Ali retakes the Hejaz in 1812 and destroys the Emirate of Diriyah in 1818.

wars.name: Greek War of Independence

zones.text: the Peloponnese and the northern Gulf of Corinth

wars.outcome: Greek victory: independence for the Peloponnese and the northern Gulf of Corinth in 1829, recognised by the London Protocol of 1830; the Egyptian fleet is lost at Navarino (20 October 1827).

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828–1829)

zones.text: the places where ground changed hands: Kars, Akhalkalaki, Akhaltsikhe, Anapa, Poti, the Danube delta and Varna

wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Adrianople; Russia occupies the Danubian principalities and receives the Black Sea coast of the Caucasus and western Georgia.
wars.note: Zones added after review from the war page: Kars (June 1828, returned), Akhalkalaki and Akhaltsikhe (July-August 1828, kept by Russia), Anapa and Poti (kept), the Danube delta (kept), Varna (September 1828, returned).

wars.name: Egyptian–Ottoman War (1831–1833)
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory at Konya (21 December 1832); the Convention of Kütahya (5 May 1833) gives Muhammad Ali the governorships of Crete, Aleppo, Tripoli, Damascus and Sidon.

wars.name: Egyptian–Ottoman War (1839–1841)
wars.outcome: Ottoman victory with British and Austrian help: Muhammad Ali accepts the London Convention (27 November 1840), keeps Egypt and Sudan as hereditary rule and renounces Crete and the Hijaz.

wars.name: Crimean War
wars.outcome: Allied and Ottoman victory: by the Treaty of Paris Russia cedes southern Bessarabia and recognises de jure Ottoman suzerainty over the Danubian principalities.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1877–1878)
wars.outcome: Russian victory: the Treaty of Berlin (13 July 1878) makes Bulgaria a vassal principality, gives full independence to Romania, Serbia and Montenegro, hands Kars, Ardahan and Batum to Russia, Bosnia to Austria-Hungary's administration and Cyprus to Britain.

wars.name: Italo-Turkish War
wars.outcome: Italian victory: the empire loses its North African territories and the Dodecanese.

wars.name: First Balkan War

zones.text: Ottoman Europe west of the Enos-Midiya line

wars.outcome: Balkan League victory: by the Treaty of London (30 May 1913) the Ottomans lose all European land west of the Enos-Midiya line and every Aegean island but Imbros and Tenedos; Albania becomes independent.

wars.name: Second Balkan War
wars.outcome: The Ottomans win back Adrianople; the Treaty of Constantinople (30 September 1913) returns Lozengrad, Lyule Burgas-Buni Hisar and Adrianople.

wars.name: Middle Eastern theatre of World War I

zones.text: north-eastern Anatolia, Iraq, Palestine and Syria

wars.outcome: Ottoman defeat: the Armistice of Mudros (30 October 1918) opens the partition; Russia captured Western Armenia in 1916 and withdrew in 1917, the British took Baghdad and Palestine in 1917 and Syria in 1918.

wars.name: Arab Revolt
wars.outcome: The revolt begins at Mecca on 10 June 1916 and expels the Ottomans from much of the Hejaz and Transjordan and takes Damascus; Hussein bin Ali founds the Kingdom of Hejaz.

wars.name: Turkish War of Independence
wars.outcome: Turkish National Movement victory: the Treaty of Sèvres (1920) is superseded at Lausanne (1923); the sultanate is abolished on 1 November 1922.

certainty.note: Beylik, march and Anatolian-interior frontiers are approximate. Treaty lines exist from the 1540s (Hungary, the 1555 Persian frontier, Zsitvatorok 1606, Zuhab 1639) but the pages opened give them as campaign results, not surveyed lines; the Hungarian, Persian and Venetian frontiers firm up in the 1690s.

The European frontiers follow treaties (Karlowitz 1699, Passarowitz 1718, Belgrade 1739, Küçük Kaynarca 1774, Jassy 1792, Bucharest 1812, Adrianople 1829, Paris 1856, Berlin 1878, London 1913) and the Russian frontier follows them to 1878. The Arabian, Yemeni, Sudanese, Libyan and Persian-Gulf frontiers stay soft throughout, as does the Egyptian frontier of Muhammad Ali's years.
Wartime fronts, the Allied occupation zones and the 1919-1922 Anatolian fronts move monthly; the drawn shape is Cliopatria's yearly outline.

notes:
Written by the Phase B research agent for batch me-10-a (2026-10-25) from 14 Wikipedia pages (the page budget of 14 was spent); the reviewer added four and the author eight more when repairing it (26 pages in sources; see 'Revisions after review' at the end). Where a verdict or event says 'Unverified: page budget', no page opened covers it and the Cliopatria shape is kept: 33 of the 133 keyframe verdicts (shapes 1482, 1487, 1492, 1502, 1507, 1512, 1645, 1648, 1662, 1727, 1776, 1780, 1783, 1788, 1796, 1797, 1814, 1815, 1822, 1824, 1825, 1828, 1853, 1856, 1857, 1859, 1866, 1870, 1871, 1895, 1900, 1905, 1911) and 51 ledger events at confidence 1 ('page silent': bridging events that describe what Cliopatria's shape adds or drops in a year, so the map shows the change).

Cliopatria rows: one continuous row, 'Ottoman Empire', 1305..1923 in 132 shapes. No row needs splitting. A new keyframe, ottoman-empire_1299, covers 1299-1304 (the 1305 core extended back to the founding, which the Rise page calls 'purely symbolic'). The 1922 shape is trimmed to 1922 only: the sultanate was abolished on 1 November 1922 and the Republic of Turkey was proclaimed on 29 October 1923, but Cliopatria's Republic of Turkey row starts in 1924, so 1923 (and the Ottoman shape drawn for it) falls between the two. The republic-of-turkey dossier should start in 1923. Cliopatria draws Ottoman Tripolitania as its own row (1840-1911, slug ottoman-tripolitania); Libya is therefore not in this dossier's shapes, and the 1911-12 Italian conquest is handled by that dossier.

Where Cliopatria's shape was adjusted: 1344-1385 (a 580-cell block of Sivas, Kayseri, Erzincan, Tokat and Yozgat added in 1344, and Constantinople, removed because the city is Byzantine until 29 May 1453; the Rise page has only Karesi 1345-6 and Cimpe 1354 before 1362, and the Anatolian beyliks page puts the advance into Anatolia 'towards the end of the 14th century'); 1395 and 1402-1450 (central Anatolia and Thessaloniki, Timur and the Interregnum); 1459-1519 (Belgrade, held by Hungary until 1521); 1529 and 1683 (Austria's Vienna); 1609 (Iraq); 1738-1769 (Azov); 1772 (Kerch); 1805-1809 (Egypt, a vassal under Muhammad Ali from 1805); 1834 and 1836 (Crete); 1922 (years only).

Disagreements between pages. (1) Thessaloniki 1387: the main article's summary says 'captured from Venice'; the Rise page has the Ottomans take it in 1387 from the Byzantines and Venice acquire it only in 1423, which the dossier follows. (2) Karaman: the Rise page has Mehmed II 'conquering and annexing' the Karamanid emirate in 1451, but Cliopatria keeps Karaman until 1467 and the Eyalet page dates the Karaman eyalet to 1468 (text) or 1483 (table); the ledger uses 1468 at confidence 2. (3) Capitals: the infobox gives Prousa from 1335 while the body says Orhan made Bursa the capital in 1326; the infobox is followed. (4) The Eyalet page's table dates Yemen to 1517, Tunis to 1524 and Algiers to 1517; these look like table groupings, not the dates of conquest, and are held at confidence 1.

Not settled, for gap-fillers. Tunisia: the Beylik of Tunis page dates the Husainid coup (July 1705) and the French protectorate (12 May 1881), so the vassal relation runs 1705-1881 (the main article says only that the Porte 'had lost Egypt, Tunisia, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Lebanon' by 1897); Cliopatria's Ottoman shape drops Tunisia in 1706. Hasa and Yemen (1873) are undated on the pages opened. The 1,213-cell Persian block that Cliopatria adds in 1727 is unsupported at confidence 1 (the Ottoman-Persian wars page lists no war between 1623-1639 and 1730-1735). The Ottoman-Persian wars page was thin; Baghdad's dates (1535, 1624, 1638) and the Amasya terms (1555) come from the main article and the Ottoman-Safavid War (1623-1639) page. The Allied occupation of Constantinople (13 November 1918 to 23 September 1923) is not recorded as a loss because the state keeps its seat and Cliopatria draws the city Ottoman to 1922. Mosul went to Iraq only in 1926, after this state ended. The Sanjak of Novi Pazar (occupied by Austria-Hungary in 1878, handed back 1908) is not in the gazetteer. No rulers list: the list of sultans was not among the 14 pages, so the `rulers` key is omitted. A reviewer who allows one more page should open the list of sultans.

Vassal pairing: Muhammad Ali's Egypt (vassal_start 1805), his Syria, Crete and Adana (vassal_start 1833) and Egypt again (vassal_start February 1841) are three starts with the counterpart muhammad-ali-dynasty, and the ends are the Levant end of November 1840 and the end of 1865 (the compiler closes the whole relation at each end, so the 1833 start is covered by the 1840 end). Fx-52 (K03) dropped the former /ledger/225, a 5 November 1914 vassal_end that named muhammad-ali-dynasty although the dynasty's own span ends in 1865: the vassalage of 1866-1914 belongs to khedivate-of-egypt, whose dossier opens it (ledger/1) and closes it (ledger/27, December 1914). The validator pairs first-in-first-out and so warns that the February 1841 start has no end; that is a counting artifact of the 1833 start inside one relation, not a missing event. The renderer should read the regions. Wallachia is a vassal from 1395 to about 1402 (confidence 1, bridging) and again from 1419 to 1878.

Counterparts with no Cliopatria row and no slug in polities.csv, which need a dossier from another group: Eastern Rumelia (1878-1885, Congress of Berlin page; the ledger draws it as the Cliopatria 1880 minus 1879 difference), Musa Celebi (the Interregnum claimant, beaten by Mehmed in 1413), the Order of St John at Tripoli (the Tripolitania eyalet of 1551; the page names no holder, so the reading is the researcher's), Bani Khalid (Hasa 1560; the page names none), the Greek lords of Thessaly and the Duchy of Athens (c. 1394-5), the Sivas-region beyliks (Eretna; no page opened names them), and the Sharifate of Mecca (Barakat submitted about eight years after 1517). The other counterparts are slugs in polities.csv whose dossiers other groups write (Safavid Dynasty, Habsburg Monarchy, Republic of Venice, Russian Empire, Principality of Wallachia, Principality of Moldavia, Muhammad Ali dynasty, Kingdom of Hungary, Kingdom of Hejaz, Republic of Turkey and the rest); the slugs were not checked for a dossier file.

The author then reopened or opened ten pages and changed the following.
